Infrastructure Engineer — Polymarket

About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform. We enable individuals to express views on real-world events by trading on outcomes across politics, economics, sports, culture, and current affairs. Built as a peer-to-peer marketplace with no centralized "house," Polymarket aggregates diverse opinions into transparent, market-based probabilities that reflect collective expectations about the future.

We're growing fast: both in volume ($21B traded in 2025) and in adoption as an alternative news source. Our ambition is to become a ubiquitous beacon of truth in global media, powered by fast, reliable, and deeply technical market infrastructure.

About the role

Polymarket is looking for an Infrastructure Engineer to help build, scale, and operate the platform that our exchange and product engineering teams run on. This role is focused on the systems underneath the systems — Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, and reliability — that let our engineers ship fast without breaking things.

You'll be a core individual contributor working with senior engineers across the org to design, automate, and harden the infrastructure that powers Polymarket at scale. This is a high-ownership role with minimal bureaucracy and a strong bias toward execution.

What you'll do

We're looking for an experienced infrastructure engineer who's comfortable owning systems end-to-end and enjoys solving hard operational and scaling problems.

  • Own core infrastructure: Design, build, and operate the Kubernetes-based platform that runs Polymarket's services, including cluster architecture, workload scheduling, and multi-environment management.

  • Build for scale & reliability: Design and implement systems for autoscaling, load balancing, service discovery, and disaster recovery that hold up under real trading volume.

  • Automate everything: Write code (not just scripts) to manage infrastructure as code, build internal tooling, and eliminate manual toil across deployment, provisioning, and operations.

  • Strengthen CI/CD: Build and maintain fast, reliable deployment pipelines that let engineering teams ship confidently and frequently.

  • Drive observability & incident response: Build monitoring, logging, and alerting systems; participate in on-call rotations and lead root-cause analysis for production incidents.

  • Manage cloud infrastructure: Architect and optimize our cloud footprint (AWS/GCP) for cost, performance, and security.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work closely with backend, exchange, and product engineering teams to ensure infrastructure decisions support the platform's performance and growth needs.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years of professional infrastructure/platform/DevOps engineering experience, ideally at a large-scale company with high-traffic, production systems.

  • Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes and Docker in production — cluster operations, workload orchestration, and container lifecycle management.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals — able to write production-grade code (Go, Python, or similar), not just configuration and scripts.

  • Solid experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS or GCP), including networking, IAM, compute, and storage.

  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code tooling (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar) and CI/CD systems.

  • Comfortable debugging complex, distributed production systems on Linux and taking ownership of correctness, performance, and uptime.

  • (Plus) Experience operating infrastructure for high-throughput, low-latency, or financial/trading systems.

  • (Plus) Experience with service mesh, GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux), or multi-cluster/multi-region architectures.

  • (Plus) Familiarity with observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry).

Benefits

  • Competitive salary & equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Full Health, Vision, & Dental coverage

  • 401k match

About the Role

Hi, I'm Kas Pawa, VP & Chief of Staff at Jane. I lead several cross-functional initiatives at Jane, including our Business Intelligence / Data & Analytics function. I also oversee operational infrastructure and executive support across our leadership team.

Here's what I've learned: executive assistants are almost invisible when they're doing their job well. But when they're missing or under-resourced, everything falls apart. Leaders spend time on logistics instead of strategy. Teams feel deprioritized. Context gets lost. The work that should amplify leadership impact instead creates friction.

What makes this role special is that it's not just calendar management - it's about creating operational infrastructure that lets leadership focus on what matters. Our Jane Leadership Team leads large teams. They're managing competing priorities across the entire company. They need someone who understands that every meeting they miss, every delayed response, every travel logistics problem sends ripples through the organization. And they need someone who can proactively solve for that.

We've built a proven approach - weekly workflows with each executive, clear communication protocols, partnership with our internal Events team - and now we're ready to scale it. We need someone who gets that this isn't about being organized and responsive (though those things matter). It's about being strategic. About understanding context without being in every meeting. About reading between the lines and saying: "Here's what I think is happening, and here's how I'd solve for it."

I'm looking for executive support as partnership work - which means resourcefulness, curiosity, and the ability to manage competing personalities and workflows without losing sight of what matters. It means seeing complexity as a puzzle to solve, not a burden. It means bringing both genuine care and strategic thinking to the role, and bringing AI into the workflow as a tool to amplify your impact.


What Impact We’re Looking for You to Make

  • Own calendar management across multiple executives with distinct personalities and working styles, creating seamless workflows that protect their time and give them breathing room to focus on what matters most.

  • Build trusted partnerships with executives through clear, consistent communication - especially in explaining the "why" behind calendar changes so teams feel supported and cared for.

  • Anticipate needs and solve problems proactively by reading between the lines, identifying which recurring meetings are moveable, and proposing solutions instead of waiting for direction.

  • Leverage AI tools thoughtfully to amplify your own impact - drafting communications, scanning calendars for patterns, researching travel and onsite logistics - then reviewing and refining before it goes out (always 90% draft, then review).

  • Partner across teams and functions - working with People Partners, team leads, our internal Events team, and external vendors - to coordinate department offsites, JLT onsites, travel logistics, and all the operational details that support leadership.

What Experience We Need

  • Approximately 5+ years of experience as an executive assistant in a fast-paced, scaling environment, with demonstrated success supporting multiple executives across different functions and personalities.

  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities with grace. Comfort working independently without frequent validation, and genuine curiosity about how to make things simpler and more efficient.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills - you draft correspondence, explain complex calendar decisions in writing, and communicate confidently across all levels. Proficiency with Google Suite (Gmail, Docs, Sheets), Slack, Notion, and comfort learning new tools quickly.

  • High emotional intelligence, resilience, and the ability to separate business realities from personal reactions. You understand that an executive's short tone usually reflects workload stress, not friction with you - and you care enough about their success that you show up and support them anyway. You need genuine empathy paired with thick skin.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and a growth mindset - this role is still evolving, and we're building the best practices together. You're someone who experiments, asks good questions, and isn't afraid to suggest better ways of doing things.

We're hiring for people based in the Vancouver area who can travel to our North Vancouver office. Being in the same geographic area opens up opportunities for in-person strategy sessions, collaborative working days, and the kind of connection that builds stronger partnerships in a remote-first company.

If you don't meet every single qualification but are excited about this role, we'd still love to hear from you.

More About Jane

Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers.

We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day - to - day lives.

Jane is growing fast, and that growth brings exciting challenges that call for adaptability, resilience, learning agility, and humility. We're proud of what we've built and quick to admit what we don't know yet. We listen, learn, and adjust as we go. More than 70,000 businesses run on Jane which has 250,000+ practitioners interacting with our product on a daily basis and growth is continuing to accelerate.

We're also embracing the possibilities of AI, using it to work smarter, improve our systems, and create even better experiences for our customers and our team. No matter your role or team, we expect every Janer to be curious, experimenting, and finding new ways to build with AI. We'll make sure you have the tools, support, and space to explore, learn, and share what you discover along the way.

Our goal isn't just delivery - it's delight. We move quickly, communicate openly, and solve real problems together. If you're energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and eager to learn with others, you'll thrive at Jane.

Compensation & Benefits

At Jane, we're committed to paying fairly, clearly, and above all, paying for growth. This role has an annual salary range of $71,600 to $107,400. While that is a large range, it is intentional. It reflects the full growth journey someone might take in the role, from developing skills early on to becoming highly proficient and ultimately achieving excellence.

Most new hires join at the accomplished stage, which for this role represents an annual salary of $89,500. A starting salary below this typically indicates a candidate with strong potential who is still developing key skills. Salaries above this usually apply to existing team members who have made a significant impact and bring deep Jane - specific knowledge.

We believe in paying for growth. You'll have regular career development conversations with your manager, and your compensation will grow as you gain experience and contribute meaningfully to our mission.

Paying clearly is one of our compensation fundamentals. Watch this short video to learn how our salary bands are set. You're also encouraged to ask questions about compensation at any point during the interview process.

We also offer a comprehensive benefits package. You can learn more about it here!


Jane takes job scams and candidate fraud seriously. Jane will only contact you from an @jane.app email address. We'll never contact you from a personal email, ask for payment, or request purchases during the hiring process. If something doesn't seem right, please reach out to us at hiring@jane.app before sharing any personal information.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is in a critical phase of growth. We grew immensely last year and are building out a talented business systems team to ensure we maintain this trajectory for years to come. You’ll work directly with our Sales, Account Management, Partnerships, and Product teams to execute mission-critical business systems projects across the organization. This is a key role where you will be uniquely positioned to impact the full picture of Ramp’s growth efforts through systems development.


What You'll Do

  • Own a GTM systems domain end to end: its roadmap, the architecture decisions inside it and its operational health

  • Build and deploy Salesforce automation end to end: record-triggered and screen flows, validation rules, custom objects and fields, permission sets and approvals

  • Translate business requirements into solution designs and write them up as the business outcome they produce rather than a list of objects and fields

  • Prioritize incoming requests against ROI. Make the call on what gets built, what gets deferred, and what gets declined, and show the numbers behind it

  • Own the dashboards and data models your domain runs on. Translate business questions into reporting that is accurate, documented and actually used to make decisions

  • Drive cross-functional alignment on scope, sequencing, and tradeoffs and carry it through to closure without a manager in the room

  • Use AI to move faster on flow logic, test cases, documentation and impact analysis and define the guardrails for how the team uses it with GTM data



What You'll Need

  • 5+ years in business systems at a fast-paced company

  • Salesforce Admin certification or equivalent hands-on experience, plus real depth in HubSpot

  • Non-trivial Salesforce flows built and debugged when they broke, and a clear view of why declarative automation goes wrong at scale

  • A habit of framing problems rather than waiting for a spec: ambiguous requests taken on, decided and shipped

  • Fluency translating business requirements into a solution, and authoring that solution in terms of the outcome it drives and how that outcome will be measured

  • A metric-driven approach to prioritization: requests ranked on ROI, effort weighed against ongoing maintenance cost and the reasoning made explicit to the requester

  • Multi-month projects delivered with cross-team dependencies and no PM attached: sequencing the work, holding scope, flagging risk before it lands, clearing blockers rather than reporting them and keeping everyone informed without being asked

  • Fluency with AI tools to build, audit and document faster and a clear sense of where they stop being reliable


Nice to Have

  • A product mindset toward internal tooling: treating stakeholders as users, shipping in phases and measuring adoption after launch

Profile
